# VRFBuildProfileSection

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Editors.Build` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/interaction/physics-hold/Editor/Build/VRFBuildProfileSection.cs#L47)

Registers the VRF settings as a section in Unity's own Build Profiles window, so a profile's
framework configuration sits next to its Player Settings and Quality rather than in a
separate window.

Unity's supported route for this is a static method marked
`[BuildProfileSettingsProvider]`, but the scan behind it keeps only types whose
assembly resolves to `RegistryType.UnityRegistry`- a built-in module, or a package
installed from the default Unity registry. Embedded, git, local and scoped-registry
packages do not qualify, and code under Assets has no package at all and is dropped
before the check. So the provider is registered directly here instead.

This is internal editor API and is expected to break eventually. It is written to fail
quietly: any step that does not find what it expects leaves the section out, records why
in [`Unavailable`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-build/VRFBuildProfileSection#unavailable), and changes nothing else. VRFramework > Build edits the
same settings either way, and no other file depends on this one.

What it relies on, verified against Unity 6000.5:

- `Handlers.AddSettingsDataProvider.s_InternalSettings`- the private static
list of built-in sections, appended to here.
- `Elements.ScriptableObjectSettingsProvider<T>`- does all the work;
its constructor takes the public descriptor below.
- `BuildProfileSettingsProvider.settingsType`- public type, internal setter,
normally filled in from the attribute.

To check it after an editor upgrade: open File > Build Profiles and look for the section,
or read [`Unavailable`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-build/VRFBuildProfileSection#unavailable) in the VRF Build window.
